text:
rachel_p: EdgeWorks SI flagged a mismatch in the on‑prem networking assumptions for Accelerator. They expect outbound egress to fetch model artifacts from our registry, but their security team prefers no direct internet egress. Need a quick architecture decision (NAT vs proxy vs local registry). Kickoff with SI tomorrow morning — who can join?

josh_s: can join. first-pass thought: two options — 1) NAT gateway with strict egress allowlist for our artifact hosts, 2) outbound proxy + authenticated pulls (more auditability). NAT is simpler but less auditable. :thinking_face:

nikita_m: @josh_s what's the required control-plane traffic? Is it just model artifacts (pulls) + telemetry, or also callbacks from our runtime? latency-sensitive infer requests must stay internal, right?

rachel_p: EdgeWorks says runtime inference will be local (no callbacks), just pulls for images + periodic model updates and metrics push. Security insisted on no 0.0.0.0/0 egress. They mentioned HSM/KMS integration too.

liam_ops: If no internet egress allowed, other option is an airgapped pull workflow: partner mirrors artifacts to a local registry (we can provide signed bundles). That requires CI changes on our side.

josh_s: mirror approach is safest but biggest lift for both sides. Could we support a jumpbox/proxy that allows outbound to a tiny allowlist (artifacts.redwood.ai, registry.redwood.ai) and TLS mutual auth? That satisfies audit and limits scope.

nikita_m: two technical constraints: 1) model artifact downloads can be 100s of MB — proxy adds latency during deployment. 2) KV/cache priming needs access to our metric endpoints for QoS telemetry. If partner blocks telemetry, we need different health signals.

rachel_p: EdgeWorks is OK with limited telemetry (aggregated metrics) but no per-token logs. They will run egress through their firewall team if we give exact IPs/FQDNs.

liam_ops: firewall checklist (ask them to allow):
```
- outbound TCP 443 to registry.redwood.ai (CIDR list we'll provide)
- outbound TCP 443 to artifacts.redwood.ai (for signed bundles)
- outbound TCP 443 to telemetry.redwood.ai (ingest, optional)
```
liam_ops: If they can't do that, we fall back to signed bundle mirror flow.

josh_s: I'll draft the minimal CIDR/FQDN list and a mutual TLS guide. Also attaching a minimal security config snippet for proxy: 
```
proxy:
  host: proxy.edge
  tls_required: true
  allowed_hosts:
    - registry.redwood.ai
    - artifacts.redwood.ai
```

rachel_p: please also note HSM key wrapping requirement for their KMS — they said keys cannot leave their network. We need to confirm if we can support CMK wrap/unwrapped images.

nikita_m: tech ask: can we sign image bundles such that partner never needs our keys? yes — we can publish signed tarballs and provide a verifier binary. That avoids key exchange. I'll put an engineering estimate: ~3 days to add bundle signing + verifier to our release pipeline.

deploy-bot: ticket created: PARTNERS-4237 — "EdgeWorks Accelerator: On‑prem egress & registry options" assigned to josh_s, nikita_m, liam_ops. Due: 3 business days.

rachel_p: thanks. Meeting tomorrow 09:00 PT with EdgeWorks SI and their security lead. Agenda: 1) present options (proxy vs mirror), 2) share CIDR/FQDN list and mutual TLS guide, 3) confirm KMS/HSM constraints. Can the three of you join?

josh_s: yes. adding slides and minimal diagrams.

nikita_m: can do, will bring a short slide on bundle signing and timeline.

liam_ops: attending. I'll bring firewall checklist and sample SG rules.

rachel_p: perfect — I'll send calendar invite and paste the docs here once ready. Need decision by EOD Friday so SI can schedule their dev work. :thumbsup:

josh_s: noted. I'll also prep a fallback plan (mirror workflow) with rough effort estimate for procurement.

rachel_p: linking docs: https://redwood.internal/partnerships/edgeworks/onprem-networking (internal)

liam_ops: quick note for meeting: ask them if their registry accepts signed tarballs over SFTP too — some partners prefer SFTP pull instead of HTTP.

nikita_m: good point. mirrors via SFTP would be simple for them but requires us to provide signed artifact package.

rachel_p: OK everyone — thanks. See you at 09:00 PT.
